text_blocks.snippet: To submit Form I-912, Request for Fee Waiver, you must file it with the USCIS application or petition for which you are requesting the fee waiver. You cannot submit Form I-912 separately or after the related application/petition has been received. The form and supporting documentation should be mailed to the address specified for the associated application or petition.
snippet_highlighted_words: file it with the USCIS application or petition for which you are requesting the fee waiver

list.title: 1. Complete Form I-912:
list.snippet: Ensure all sections of the form are filled out accurately and completely, including all required signatures and supporting documentation.

list.title: 2. Gather Supporting Documents:
list.snippet: You'll need to provide documentation to support your fee waiver request, such as evidence of income, household size, and any relevant financial hardship.

list.title: 3. Attach to Application/Petition:
list.snippet: Form I-912 is not filed separately. It must be attached to the specific USCIS application or petition for which you are seeking a fee waiver.

list.title: 4. Mail Together:
list.snippet: Send the completed Form I-912, the application/petition, and all supporting documents to the correct USCIS address for that application/petition.

list.title: 5. Do not send a fee:
list.snippet: If the fee waiver is granted, you will not need to pay the fee associated with the application/petition.

list.title: 6. Do not file after:
list.snippet: Form I-912 must be submitted at the same time as the related application/petition. It cannot be filed separately or after the application/petition has been received.

text_blocks.snippet: Form I-193, Application for Waiver of Passport and/or Visa, is used by nonimmigrant aliens seeking admission to the United States to request a waiver of passport and/or visa requirements due to unforeseen emergencies. It can also be used by returning lawful permanent residents (LPRs) who have temporarily traveled abroad and need a waiver of documentary requirements.
snippet_highlighted_words: used by nonimmigrant aliens seeking admission to the United States to request a waiver of passport and/or visa requirements due to unforeseen emergencies

list.snippet: Purpose: To request a waiver of passport and/or visa requirements.
Who uses it: Nonimmigrant aliens and returning LPRs.
When it's used: When an individual encounters an unforeseen emergency or has a legitimate reason for not having the required documents.
Where it's filed: At the port of entry or during the immigration process.
Fee: A fee of $695 (USD) is generally required, but can be waived on a case-by-case basis by a CBP officer.
Authority: Sections 212(a)(7), 212(d)(4), and 212(k) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, as amended.
Examples: A medical emergency, loss of documents within 48 hours of departure, or a situation where a visa was cancelled.
